Subject: Reconcile scoring discrepancy — Becky Owens (Senior Infra)

Team,

Thanks again for covering Becky’s loop this morning. I pulled the panel_scorecard.xlsx into the Drive folder (link below) and noticed a pretty wide spread on system-design and scalability — Monica has Becky at a 2 on design while others scored 4s. That gap will block a clean green/red decision in Greenhouse.

Quick context: Becky has strong infra ops background (see resume attached) and solid production debugging examples; the divergence is largely around detailed sharding/partitioning strategy and tradeoffs for multi-region KV stores.

Ask: please reply in-thread with either: 1) a one-line calibration note (what rubric item drove your score), and 2) your final recommendation (Hire / Hire-with-conditions / No-hire). If you can, update the annotated column in panel_scorecard.xlsx too. I’d like to lock the panel consensus by 5pm PT today so we can communicate to recruiting.

Links & attachments:
- Candidate profile: https://greenhouse.io/candidate/ACME-12345
- Panel scorecard (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDefGHI
- Attachments: becky_owens_resume.pdf, panel_scorecard.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll lane any tie-break follow-ups if needed.

-Markus

On Sun, 23 Aug 2026 at 09:12, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
>
> Thanks again for covering Becky’s loop this morning. I pulled the panel_scorecard.xlsx into the Drive folder (link below) and noticed a pretty wide spread on system-design and scalability — Monica has Becky at a 2 on design while others scored 4s. That gap will block a clean green/red decision in Greenhouse.

Thanks for pulling this together. My quick calibration note:
- Rubric item: System design — scalability & partitioning.
- Why 2: Becky’s answers were strong on incident response and observability, but when pressed on partitioning she proposed eventual-consistent sharding heuristics without concrete rebalancing approaches (no worked example for reducing cross-region hot-shard traffic). For Senior Infra I expect explicit partition migration/reshard strategies and tradeoffs.

Recommendation: No-hire as Senior; would consider hire at Staff (individual contributor focused on runbook improvements) only if she demonstrates deeper design tradeoffs in a follow-up take-home.

Attachment: I added inline comments to panel_scorecard.xlsx (column: MONICA_NOTES).

—Monica

Subject: Re: Reconcile scoring discrepancy — Becky Owens (Senior Infra)

Thanks for the clear notes, Monica. I took a pass at consolidating the numeric scores into a proposed panel score (see column: PROPOSED_PANEL_SCORE in the scorecard). My high-level synthesis:
- Ops & debugging: unanimous 4
- System design: split (2,4,4) -> proposed 3 with note “needs design work”
- Culture & collaboration: 4

Proposed panel recommendation: Hire, level: Senior, with a conditional ask — require a short take-home focused on partitioning & rebalancing (2-3 hours) to be completed before final offer. We treat this as a risk-mitigation step rather than a full bar-raising retake.

If anyone objects to that approach, please reply with a one-line veto + reason. Otherwise I’ll mark the panel hire-with-conditions in Greenhouse and tell recruiting to move to reference checks.

Drive candidate notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDefGHI
Greenhouse: https://greenhouse.io/candidate/ACME-12345

Subject: Re: Reconcile scoring discrepancy — Becky Owens (Senior Infra)

Short note — I defer to Markus on the architecture judgment and to Monica on depth expectations. After rereading notes and the quick convo with Becky, I’m comfortable with Laura’s conservative path: Hire with conditions (take-home focused on sharding/rebalancing). My only add: include an explicit success criterion for the take-home (clear explanation of tradeoffs + one worked migration example).

Final recommendation: Hire-with-conditions (Senior), contingent on satisfactory take-home.

-Rishi
